title: The digit split — 19 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
The digit split — 19 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the ring. 19 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide). Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 6 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 64 pair(s); the theorems fall into 4 strand(s), the largest of 16. Most binding: tokens (10), coinStep (5), coins (4), singles (2), isUnit9 (2), sealBits (2). 3 theorem(s) name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file(s): src/proof/split.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 19 sealed receipts fold to f2559dc3-4948-8db4-b488-b9d61eaf226e. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (1, 1, 4, 8, 4, 0, 3). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: demand2.lean (5 observed, 1.69 expected, lift 2.97), theorems.lean (4 observed, 1.69 expected, lift 2.37), families.lean (17 observed, 8.85 expected, lift 1.92). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.42; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.58. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 35.5% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. the classification this file rests on is standard and is credited: the units of ℤ/9 are {1,2,4,5,7,8} and the non-units {0,3,6}, exactly the residues coprime to 9. That is textbook abstract algebra — Wikipedia's "multiplicative group of integers modulo n", and every algebra course. So `the_singles_are_exactly_the_non_units` and `the_pairs_are_exactly_the_units_in_order` RESTATE known mathematics and claim nothing. Stated precisely so the credit does not run past the earlier work: what is NOT claimed as prior art is the tokenisation itself — reading the digits as 0|12|3|45|6|78|9 by concatenating consecutive units into two-digit tokens, and the arithmetic that follows from it (every token a multiple of three, closure of the tokens under addition and multiplication). That arrangement is this deposit's presentation of a standard fact, and its verification is by exhaustion here. Crediting an earlier author for a presentation they did not make is the same defect as claiming their result, pointed the other way. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. the_singles_are_exactly_the_non_units — ((List.range 10).filter (fun d => ! isUnit9 d)) = [0, 3, 6, 9] ∧ singles = [0, 3, 6, 9] record
  2. the_pairs_are_exactly_the_units_in_order — ((List.range 10).filter isUnit9) = unitsOf9 ∧ unitsOf9 = [1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8] record
  3. each_pair_is_two_consecutive_units — 12 = 1 * 10 + 2 ∧ 45 = 4 * 10 + 5 ∧ 78 = 7 * 10 + 8 ∧ 2 = 1 + 1 ∧ 5 = 4 + 1 ∧ 8 = 7 + 1 record
  4. every_token_is_a_multiple_of_three — tokens.all (fun t => t % 3 == 0) record
  5. the_tokens_are_three_times_these — tokens.map (fun t => t / 3) = [0, 4, 1, 15, 2, 26, 3] record
  6. addition_and_multiplication_stay_inside — tokens.all (fun a => tokens.all (fun b => (a + b) % 3 == 0 && (a * b) % 3 == 0)) record
  7. subtraction_stays_inside — tokens.all (fun a => tokens.all (fun b => a < b || (a - b) % 3 == 0)) record
  8. division_is_the_operation_that_leaves — 12 / 3 = 4 ∧ 4 % 3 != 0 ∧ 45 / 9 = 5 ∧ 5 % 3 != 0 ∧ 6 / 3 = 2 ∧ 2 % 3 != 0 record
  9. the_roots_are_the_singles — tokens.map (fun t => t % 9) = [0, 3, 3, 0, 6, 6, 0] record
  10. every_root_is_a_single — tokens.all (fun t => singles.contains (if t % 9 == 0 then (if t == 0 then 0 else 9) else t % 9)) record
  11. the_coin_step_and_the_coins_are_inverse — ((List.range 20).all (fun c => 3 * c / 3 == c && (3 * c) % 3 == 0)) ∧ coinStep = 3 * coins ∧ coinStep / 3 = coins record
  12. paying_and_refunding_coins_on_the_last_pair_round_trips — ((List.range 27).all (fun k => 3 * (26 - k) + 3 * k == 78)) ∧ 3 * (26 - coins) = 72 ∧ 72 = 8 * 9 record
  13. the_exhaustible_tokens_are_those_six_divides — (tokens.filter (fun t => t % coinStep == 0)) = [0, 12, 6, 78] record
  14. the_rest_halt_on_the_generator — (tokens.filter (fun t => t % coinStep != 0)) = [3, 45, 9] ∧ (tokens.filter (fun t => t % coinStep != 0)).all (fun t => t % coinStep == 3) record
  15. every_token_is_void_bound_or_halts_on_three — tokens.all (fun t => t % coinStep == 0 || t % coinStep == 3) record
  16. inside_this_ideal_the_bare_coin_sorts_as_the_scaled_one — (tokens.filter (fun t => t % 2 == 0)) = (tokens.filter (fun t => t % coinStep == 0)) ∧ tokens.all (fun t => (t % 2 == 0) == (t % coinStep == 0)) record
  17. a_seal_divides_into_payments_and_multiplies_back — ([1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128].all (fun c => (sealBits / c) * c == sealBits && sealBits / (sealBits / c) == c)) ∧ sealBits / coins = 2 ^ 6 record
  18. sixty_four_is_where_the_doubling_returns — (2 ^ 6) % 9 = 1 ∧ ((List.range 6).map (fun k => (2 ^ k) % 9)) = [1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5] ∧ ((List.range' 1 5).all (fun k => (2 ^ k) % 9 != 1)) record
  19. the_orbit_turns_once_per_budget — ((List.range 60).all (fun n => 2 ^ (n + 6) % 9 == 2 ^ n % 9)) ∧ 2 ^ 6 = sealBits / coins record
